classificationReport.tier3Note: Tier-3 (forge + Medusa) CONFIRMED >=2:1 over-collateralized backing and that decimal math cannot over-mint under correct deployment. No value-at-risk path lifts any finding to Medium. Each finding's worst case is either an owner deploy/wiring footgun (recoverable / detectable / no external attacker) or a transparency/spec nit.
classificationReport.noInflationStatement: All 6 sanitizer pre-assessments verified against source (Uniboost.sol, UniboostMintDebtHook.sol, ATokenDispatcherV2.sol, DefaultDispatchHook.sol). None warrants escalation to Medium or High. The one over-mint tail (DEDUP-13-002) is an owner deploy-config footgun with no external/runtime attacker requirement, so it does not satisfy the C4 Medium 'value leak with external requirements via attack path' bar; it remains Low under Law-1 recall-keep.

classifiedFinding.title: Uniboost has no hookTypeId guard: an unwired/wrong dispatch hook silently accrues zero phUSD debt (M-04 fail-open class reborn on a third dispatcher)
classifiedFinding.plausibility: n/a (owner-config dependent, not an attacker scenario)

classification.assetImpact: No theft and no direct loss of held assets. Impact is a backing-integrity feature failure: if the owner leaves the constructor-default DefaultDispatchHook (onDispatch is an empty no-op, confirmed src/hooks/DefaultDispatchHook.sol:12) or wires a mismatched hook, every Uniboost dispatch forwards prime with ZERO phUSD mint-debt accrued. phUSD that should have been backed by accrued debt simply is never accrued; no existing balance is removed.
attackPath: 1. Owner deploys Uniboost; base ATokenDispatcherV2 ctor sets hook = new DefaultDispatchHook() (no-op).
2. Owner opens dispatches WITHOUT calling setHook(uniboostMintDebtHook) (or sets the wrong hook).
3. ATokenDispatcherV2._dispatch calls hook.onDispatch unconditionally (no hookTypeId marker check, unlike the M-04-fixed NudgeRatchet) -> no debt accrues, no revert, no event.
4. Backing accounting for Uniboost-routed prime is silently zero until the owner notices and fixes the wiring.
classification.likelihood: low-to-moderate operational; requires an owner setup omission. No external/permissionless trigger.
classification.assumptions: Owner forgets/mis-wires setHook on the new dispatcher. The base contract genuinely lacks a hookTypeId guard on this path (verified).
classification.externalRequirements: None beyond the owner config omission; no attacker, no market condition.
classification.recoverable: Yes. setHook can be corrected at any time; only debt that should have accrued during the unwired window is lost-not-accrued (no retroactive backfill), but the prime itself is retained on-chain.

classifiedFinding.justification: C4 Low/QA: this is a non-obvious owner operational hazard (Law-3 footgun, NOT obvious misconfig and NOT a malicious-owner vector, so KI#4 does not suppress it). It is the third dispatcher to copy the M-04-vulnerable unconditional-hook pattern and is the dispatcher most analogous to the M-04-FIXED NudgeRatchet. Same fail-open class as owner-accepted wont-fix Q-08 (BalancerPoolerV2), but on a distinct contract/function => distinct fingerprint => NOT auto-suppressed; routed for explicit owner decision. No direct asset risk, no protocol-availability break (dispatch still functions), recoverable => stays Low, NOT Medium.
classifiedFinding.borderlineNote: Considered Medium under 'protocol function impacted' — rejected: the dispatch function still operates; only an optional accounting side-effect is skipped, and it is recoverable and owner-triggered with no external requirement. Medium would overstate it.
classifiedFinding.precedent: Q-08 (96c60b72, owner wont-fix) — same fail-open class on BalancerPoolerV2. Sanitizer proposes wont-fix-per-Q08 (proposal only; not authoritative here).

classifiedFinding.title: UniboostMintDebtHook.scale derived from the hook's own ctor primeToken_ with no on-chain tie to the dispatcher primeToken(); decimals mismatch mis-scales all debt
classifiedFinding.plausibility: n/a (owner deploy-config dependent, not an attacker scenario)

classification.assetImpact: Two directions. UNDER-scale (hook primeToken_ has MORE decimals than the real dispatcher prime, e.g. hook=18dp, dispatcher=6dp USDC): scale too small => debt under-stated => fails safe (over-backed, no loss). OVER-scale (hook primeToken_ has FEWER decimals than the real dispatcher prime): scale too large => debt over-stated => a later pull() mints MORE phUSD than ratio*amount warrants => UNBACKED phUSD over-mint. The over-scale direction is the Law-1 tail that mandates keeping this finding even at Low.
attackPath: 1. Owner deploys UniboostMintDebtHook passing dispatcher_ and primeToken_ as two separate, same-typed address args.
2. Owner passes a primeToken_ whose decimals() differ from the dispatcher's actual _primeToken (Uniboost.sol:89) — both args type-check, neither is on-chain cross-validated.
3. scale = 10**(18 - wrongDecimals) is baked immutable at line 89.
4. Every onDispatch accrues debt at the wrong scale; if scale is too large, pull() later mints unbacked phUSD.
classification.likelihood: low; requires a deploy-time mismatch of two owner-supplied args in a single atomic deployment. No runtime path, no external attacker, no permissionless trigger. Mis-scale is detectable on the first dispatch (DebtAccrued amounts off by orders of magnitude).
classification.assumptions: Owner mis-binds primeToken_ at deploy. Decimal MATH itself is correct and guarded (d<=18, M-03 generalization) and is explicitly NOT re-raised.
classification.externalRequirements: None — there is no external/attacker requirement; the only actor is the deploying owner.
classification.recoverable: Partially. scale is immutable, so an over-scaled hook must be replaced (deploy a new hook + setDispatcher/setHook re-wire). phUSD already over-minted via pull() during the window is the irrecoverable portion; the mis-scale is detectable before pull() if monitored.

classifiedFinding.justification: LOW, not Medium — explicit C4 reasoning. C4 Medium = 'leak value with a hypothetical attack path with stated assumptions, but external requirements.' Here there is NO external requirement and NO attack path: the sole actor is the deploying owner, and the trigger is a one-time deploy-config mismatch of two args the owner fully controls, detectable on the first dispatch before any pull(). That is the textbook definition of a deploy-config footgun (Law-3, non-obvious because the M-03/M-04 fixes would lead an owner to assume the scale is bound to the dispatcher), not a latent Medium. The unbacked-over-mint tail is real and is why the finding is KEPT under Law-1 recall-beats-tidiness rather than dropped — but the absence of any non-owner/runtime path keeps it below the Medium bar. Tier-3 fuzzing independently confirmed the math cannot over-mint under correct deployment and backing stays >=2:1, removing any value-at-risk path under intended config.
classifiedFinding.borderlineNote: This was the deliberately-scrutinized borderline. Argument FOR Medium: over-scale mints unbacked phUSD (real value leak). Argument FOR Low (adopted): no external requirement, no attacker, no runtime trigger; single atomic owner deploy error; detectable pre-pull; over-scale is the rarer of two directions (the default/expected USDC-6dp deployment under-scales-safe if anything is wrong). A C4 judge would not grant Medium for an owner-only deploy mismatch with no external attack surface. Remediation collapses it entirely: one ctor assertion tying scale to the dispatcher's primeToken().
classifiedFinding.remediation: Add a constructor assertion: require(IERC20Metadata(IUniboost(dispatcher_).primeToken()).decimals() == d) (or derive d directly from the dispatcher's primeToken()), removing the dual-arg ambiguity.
classifiedFinding.precedent: Open ledger L-07 (ac91a046) — same decimal-config family on a different surface (replaceDispatcher stale price). Cross-reference at report time; distinct fingerprint, do not merge.

classifiedFinding.title: setPool repoints _pairToken without re-validating stored custom _primeToPairPath (stale path can route swap to wrong token)

classification.assetImpact: No theft, no silent value leak. A stored custom _primeToPairPath whose end token no longer matches the repointed _pairToken would route the next pool() swap toward the wrong token — but this is loud: the next pool() reverts or under-funds against its on-chain minPairOut/minTargetOut floors, and any stranded dust is sweepable via rescueERC20.
attackPath: 1. Owner sets a custom _primeToPairPath ending at the current pair token.
2. Owner later calls setPool to repoint _pairToken without clearing/re-asserting the stored path.
3. The setter silently violates its own advertised invariant (path end == pairToken).
4. Next pool() routes against the stale path -> reverts/under-funds (loud), no silent loss.
classification.likelihood: low; owner-driven, near the obvious line.
classification.assumptions: Owner uses a custom path then repoints the pair without clearing it.
classification.recoverable: Yes; re-set the path, sweep dust via rescueERC20.

classifiedFinding.justification: C4 QA: incorrect state handling — the setter breaks its own advertised path-end==pairToken invariant across setPool. No asset theft, no silent value leak (failure is loud and recoverable), so QA is correct. Not suppressed under KI#1/KI#4: a non-malicious owner could be surprised the stored path is not re-validated (non-obvious enough to surface), but the impact ceiling is a revert/dust, so it stays a QA-bundle note, not Low/Medium. Remediation: clear or re-assert _primeToPairPath inside _setPool when the pair token changes.
classifiedFinding.borderlineNote: Considered Low — rejected: impact is a revert/under-fund against on-chain floors plus sweepable dust, which is state-handling QA, not a value-leak Low.

classifiedFinding.title: Uniboost pool() buy-and-pool LP-add MEV (off-chain pooler floors only) - Uniboost instance of L-06

classification.assetImpact: Bounded MEV slippage on protocol-owned-liquidity (POL) LP adds. Worst case is value-leak-to-MEV on the single-sided pool() add, bounded by the keeper-supplied minPairOut/minTargetOut and the post-call minLP floor. Not user funds; POL only; operator-triggered.
attackPath: 1. Authorized pooler calls pool() with off-chain-computed min floors.
2. A sandwicher manipulates the pool around the add within the slack between the off-chain floor and true price (no on-chain oracle/TWAP reference).
3. The add executes at a worse rate; the delta is captured by the MEV bot, bounded by the supplied floors + minLP.
classification.likelihood: low; bounded by operator-set floors; only the slack between floor and true price is exploitable.
classification.assumptions: Operator sets loose floors; mempool is observable.
classification.recoverable: n/a (realized slippage, but bounded and POL-only).

classifiedFinding.justification: C4 Low: value leak to MEV bounded by on-chain floors (minPairOut/minTargetOut + post-call minLP), POL-only, operator-triggered, not user-facing. Same root-cause class as OPEN ledger L-06 (BalancerPoolerV2.pool off-chain-min-only LP-add MEV). econ-scanner concurs; static-analyzer unused-return/timestamp/zero-min flags fold in as benign-by-design corroboration. L-06 is open (not fixed) => NOT a regression. Stays Low; does not reach Medium because impact is bounded and confined to POL.
classifiedFinding.dedupNote: Same class as open L-06. Reuse L-06 fingerprint (342075df) as a second instance; do not mint a parallel Low. Fall back to a new Low fp cross-referencing L-06 only if finding-manager refuses cross-contract fp reuse. Severity Low either way.

classifiedFinding.title: Uniboost donationSplit <-> UniboostMintDebtHook.ratio cross-contract decoupling - Uniboost instance of L-05

classification.assetImpact: No solvency break. The donationSplit (Uniboost) and the debt ratio (hook) are set on two different contracts with no on-chain coupling invariant. Edge cases 0%/100% verified SAFE. ratio is hard-capped at MAX_RATIO=50, so worst-case accrued debt is <=50% of dispatched prime while retained value is ~100% at dispatch => backing buffer holds. Impact is a transparency/config-coupling gap, not a value-at-risk path.
attackPath: 1. Owner sets donationSplit and hook.ratio independently across two contracts.
2. No invariant ties them; a mismatched pair is silently accepted.
3. Worst case: <=50% debt vs ~100% retained value -> still over-backed (no break).
classification.likelihood: low; owner-config; bounded by the ratio<=50 cap.
classification.assumptions: Owner sets the two params inconsistently.

classifiedFinding.justification: C4 Low: non-obvious owner transparency/coupling footgun (Law-3), no asset theft and no solvency break — the ratio<=50 hard cap means worst case is <=50% debt against ~100% retained value, leaving a conservative buffer (Tier-3 confirms >=2:1). Same root-cause class as OPEN ledger L-05 (BalancerPoolerV2 batchDonationSize <-> Hook.ratio). Do NOT escalate above Low. L-05 open => no regression.
classifiedFinding.dedupNote: Same class as open L-05. Reuse L-05 fingerprint (e527a712) as a second instance; annotate L-05 with the Uniboost mirror. Fall back to a new Low fp cross-referencing L-05 only if cross-contract reuse is refused. Severity Low either way.

classifiedFinding.title: UniboostMintDebtHook.setRatio accepts ratio == MAX_RATIO vs 'strictly <' NatSpec - recurrence of L-02 class

classification.assetImpact: None. setRatio uses `if (newRatio > MAX_RATIO) revert` (line 97), so ratio == MAX_RATIO (50) is accepted, contradicting the NatSpec 'strictly less than MAX_RATIO' (line 30/95). Caps at 50% debt either way; no asset impact, no solvency change. Pure spec-vs-code boundary nit.
attackPath: 1. Owner calls setRatio(50).
2. Code accepts it (> not >=), NatSpec says it should be strictly <50.
3. Effective max debt is exactly 50% instead of <50% — still within the safe buffer.

classifiedFinding.justification: C4 QA: byte-identical spec-vs-code boundary nit to OPEN/qa-bundled ledger L-02 (BalancerPoolerMintDebtHook.setRatio). No asset impact; effective cap is 50% vs <50%, both inside the >=2:1 buffer. Tagged faithfulness:true (a documented-behavior deviation from the NatSpec invariant) and routed to spec-conformance per Law-2, but it ALSO has zero security impact so it sits at QA in the QA bundle as well — it is surfaced (not buried) via its faithfulness tag, satisfying Law-2.
classifiedFinding.faithfulnessRouting: Behavioural deviation from stated NatSpec invariant; surface in spec-conformance report (matches L-02's existing F-tagging family) AND QA bundle. Not dropped into gas noise.
classifiedFinding.dedupNote: Reuse L-02 fingerprint (5425119c) as a same-class QA instance, or a new QA item cross-referencing L-02 if L-02's fp is keyed strictly to BalancerPoolerMintDebtHook. L-02 already qa-bundled => no status change.
